## What it is

The outer grille of the scale tray, after Profitec's version 2: a flat 2.5 mm plate lying on the tray's two side rails and on its front wall, with a front apron that hangs in front of the tray's front wall. A chamfered square cut-out leaves the cup grille (`scale_grille_inner`) free, a round opening lets the purge water through onto the tray's sloping rear, and a square pull hole at the front-right corner is where a finger lifts it. Drain holes everywhere else. Modelled in the machine frame and returned through `scale_frame`, then `scale_flip`: it prints top face down, on the A1 mini (168.4 x 162.7 x 28.5 mm). Bambu PETG Basic.

## Design notes

All positions come from `scale_layout()` (`grille_outer` and `tray`).

- Plate: Z 46.0 to 48.5, X 12.3 to 180.7 (0.3 play per side inside the tray's walls), Y -20.2 to 142.5. The tray has no rear wall any more: its rear is a 45° slope whose inner face is at Y -20.5 at the plate's underside (Z 46), and the plate's rear edge, vertical, stands 0.3 in front of that point. It bears, measured, on 424 mm² of each side rail and 421 of the front wall top (its full 2.5 width). Grille and tray share zero volume.
- Apron: 2.5 thick, inner face at Y 140.0 (0.5 in front of the tray's front wall), from the plate's top down to Z 20, over the full width. It stays 3 mm above the base plate's front lip (Z 17). The user pulls the grille toward themself by the pull hole; the apron is what stops it against the tray when it is pushed back.
- Inside corner between plate and apron: square. The tray's front wall top is square now (it is the tray's bed edge), so a fill there has only the 0.5 apron gap minus the 0.3 play to live in, 0.2 mm, under the 0.8 chamfer floor.
- Cut-out: 94 square on the tower axis (97, 54), corners chamfered 5: 2 mm all round the 90 mm cup grille (measured gap 2.0, no shared volume).
- Purge opening: Ø16 at (96.5, -8), Y -16 to 0. The tray's slope spans Y -20.5 (at the plate) to -2 (where it meets the plateau's floor), so the opening is over the slope except its last 2 mm, over the plateau's flat; the machine's purge hole (Y about -9.7 to 0) drops onto the slope.
- Pull hole: 20 square, 10 in from the plate's right edge and from the tray front wall's inner face: X 150.7 to 170.7, Y 107 to 127.
- Drain holes: 8 mm squares, 3.5 webs (pitch 11.5), columns symmetric about the tray's centre line X 96.5, rows lined up on the tower axis Y 54. Only whole holes are kept, at least 6 mm in from the plate's sides and rear edge and from the tray front wall's inner face, and at least 4 mm from the cut-out, the purge opening and the pull hole. 66 holes, spanning X 23.5 to 169.5 and Y -7.5 to 127: every one over the open tub, clear of the rails (inner edge X 15 / 178), the slope's rim and the front wall. Because the columns follow the tray's centre (96.5) and the cut-out the tower axis (97), the side borders around the cut-out differ by 0.5 mm.
- Polish: 1 mm on the straight convex edges of the outline and the apron, none in the top face (the bed once flipped) and none in the underside that rests on the rails; the holes stay sharp.

## Don't

- Do not chamfer the top face: it is the bed face.
- Do not chamfer the plate's underside edges along the rails: they bear on them.
- Do not put back a fill in the plate-apron corner: with the tray's front wall top square, anything over 0.2 hits the tray.
- Do not let a drain hole sit over the front wall or a rail: water has to fall inside the tray.
- Do not slant the rear edge to follow the slope: it would lay a knife edge in the bed face once flipped.
